study.question: Does explicit auxiliary-union task-mask routing improve validation click AUC beyond aligned historical item fields and action codes in the strongest visible model, and is any effect due to event assignment rather than block-level frequency?
study.hypothesis: The inherited union of cart/fav/buy masks may provide a useful routing inductive bias despite being derived from already-supplied action codes. Conditional utility remains unestablished. Full membership may improve training via membership-dependent Dice populations and auxiliary histories; the inherited click evaluation readout itself is uniform and does not directly read feedback strata.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary text lines 75-85 describes target-conditioned local activation. This study retains the inherited action-aware scorer and contrasts explicit membership grouping; it does not claim a new local activation method or exact DIN reproduction.

Pinned primary benchmark implementation lines 123-159 initializes task-specific hubs with multi_masks. This study instead isolates union-mask grouping inside an existing block-compressed scorer with matched modules. Original INFNet paper detail is unavailable in the authorized archive; no original-paper equivalence or novelty claim.

Pinned source lines 112-144 uses a target-aware shared summary and token mixing. Considered as a shared-summary alternative, but adding a token mixer would confound this membership intervention; no mixer is introduced.

inherited_components: Exact source/config of g3-r0065-fixed_angle_cycle_source_bit_negative as a fresh full-membership utility control
Action-aware local activation; 10 blocks with uniform/feedback strata; attached rotated target-match support with folded training and pruned evaluation
Target-match detail and ordinal/quadratic moments, private residual adapters, context/history product modules, all four towers
Existing orthogonal occupied-cycle-source surrogate VJP and four-task true-label objective, preserved verbatim; this is not an ordinary joint-BCE gradient
study.proposed_difference: Change only representation use of host masks. Blind replaces feedback/complement rows by duplicate uniform block means with half/half soft counts independent of mask values. Counts-only replaces their means by the uniform block mean but retains actual per-block union counts and empty-row gates. Permuted jointly rotates all four mask bits by half the valid-event count inside each fixed block before the inherited union operation. Full control is the byte-identical imported source. No new parameters. This tests explicit auxiliary-union routing, not distinct individual-task assignments or new information beyond actions.
predictions: If event assignment is useful, full exceeds both counts-only and permuted click AUC under paired host seeds; counts-only versus blind diagnoses frequency/empty-pattern utility.
If masks mainly encode block frequency, counts-only approaches full and exceeds blind; this is not evidence for useful event assignment.
All arms have 32192421 parameters (31793216 embedding, 399205 dense) if the inherited host count reproduces; training/inference runtime must be remeasured.

At a shared checkpoint in evaluation, click predictions are invariant to membership intervention within numerical tolerance because uniform rows are unchanged; auxiliary predictions may vary. Differences in trained click predictions must arise through training.
The joint permutation preserves per-block per-task counts, joint bit-pattern multiset, valid positions and union counts; blind and counts-only never move or alter historical item/action content.
falsifiers: Full failing to exceed either counts-only or permuted across a repeated discriminating paired comparison undermines useful explicit event assignment in this model.
Counts-only matching full while both exceed blind attributes the effect to frequency/empty support, not aligned event assignment.
Apparent improvements that fail parameter, initialization, validity, cost or normalization-scope audits are uninterpretable and require repair before further trials.

Any mask sensitivity of blind predictions/gradients at fixed item/action inputs, changed padded-value sensitivity, nonfinite outputs/gradients, or mismatched inherited full source invalidates the intervention.
alternative_explanations: Actions already determine membership, so a blind model can relearn membership; no difference establishes redundancy only for this representation and training exposure.

Different scorer input distributions and Dice running moments are consequences of regrouping; a positive result cannot separate normalization from auxiliary-gradient mediation without a follow-up factorial.
Blind uses half/half soft counts, whereas full/counts-only preserve true sparsity; their contrast includes frequency, empty-row patterns and value allocation.
Deterministic within-block half-rotation is an imperfect negative control: it preserves coarse temporal frequency and can leave homogeneous or short blocks unchanged.
Single-seed effects and repeated user exposures can be misleading; earlier ancestor failures and trajectories beyond the two imported receipts are unavailable, not assumed successful or refuted.
Inherited gradient transformation may interact with auxiliary representation changes; keep its code fixed and restrict claims to this incumbent.
